# Reference Ingestion

## Purpose

Let the user bring their own images — style frames, actor or character
lookalikes, location photos, prop shots, mood boards — and convert what those
images actually show into the scaffold's structured canon: style-bible
vocabulary, `LOOK_*` assets, character/location/prop bible entries, and
registered reference assets with provenance. The user's images become the
seed of the visual system instead of the pipeline generating one from prose
alone.

## Use When

- The user drops material of any kind into `production/references/inbox/` —
  images, video clips, audio tracks, text documents — or points at
  files/URLs and says "this is the look", "she looks like this", "this is
  the apartment", "the score should feel like this".
- `/ingest-references` is invoked.
- `/visual-development` finds inbox material it should analyze before
  generating masters from scratch.

## Inputs

- The images themselves, read directly (multimodal analysis — the assistant
  looks at the pixels, not at the filename).
- The user's intent per image or batch: which entity it belongs to
  (character, wardrobe, location, prop, style/look, lighting, composition)
  and how binding it is (inspiration vs. canon).
- Existing bibles and style bible, to detect conflicts.
- Origin and license status per image (`rules/common/asset-provenance.md`).

## Process

1. Inventory the batch and ask once for anything unclassifiable; never guess
   whether an image is canon or mood.
2. Analyze each image for what it actually shows, in extractable terms:
   - **Style/look:** palette (dominant and accent colors), lighting logic
     (source, direction, hardness, time of day), texture and grain, lens
     cues (apparent focal band, depth of field, distortion, anamorphic
     artifacts), era markers, composition habits.
   - **Character:** facial geometry, hair, build, distinguishing marks,
     apparent age, wardrobe items visible, and which of it is identity vs.
     costume.
   - **Location:** geography and scale, architecture, materials, dressing,
     light states, camera-relevant sightlines.
   - **Prop:** form, material, wear state, scale cues, reading distance.
3. Write the extraction into canon, per type: style analyses become or
   extend a `LOOK_*` asset (with `prompt_vocabulary` and
   `negative_vocabulary` like `templates/looks/`) and style-bible pillars;
   character/location/prop analyses fill the matching bible entry's
   canonical description fields.
4. Register each file as a reference asset: proper ID
   (`CHAR_*/LOC_*/PROP_*/LOOK_*` per naming conventions), file moved from
   `inbox/` to its home — entity `refs/` for visual material,
   `characters/<ID>/voice/` for voice samples, `references/audio|video|docs/`
   for music refs, motion clips, and text documents — registry entry with
   `status: draft`, and provenance recorded — provider `external`, origin,
   license status. Uncleared or unknown-license files are flagged
   immediately.
5. Non-visual kinds are handled honestly: text documents are read and
   analyzed like images; audio and video files are cataloged (the assistant
   cannot hear or watch them) — the user supplies the one-line description
   ("slow build, sparse piano, tension without release"), which becomes the
   registry entry's note, and `/music-brief` or the style bible cites the
   file by path.
6. Detect conflicts instead of merging silently: an ingested image that
   contradicts an approved bible fact or style pillar (different eye color,
   different palette temperature) is reported as a decision for the user —
   supersede the canon or demote the image to inspiration.
7. Hand off: recommend which ingested assets should be promoted to `_MASTER`
   directly (the user's image IS the canon) and which should condition
   `/visual-development` generation (image-to-image toward a consistent
   master set). Promotion itself follows `draft → review → approved`.

## Outputs

- Bible entries and style-bible/LOOK updates derived from the analyses, in
  the user's project — schema-valid, `status: draft`.
- Registered reference assets with provenance and license fields, files
  organized under their entities' `refs/` directories.
- A conflict report where imported material disagrees with existing canon.
- A promotion plan: direct-to-master candidates vs. generation conditioning.

## Quality Bar

- Every extracted claim is visible in the image; no invented backstory,
  no traits the pixels don't show.
- Style vocabulary is prompt-ready and concrete (per `LOOK_*` preset
  conventions), not adjectives ("teal-and-sodium night palette, single hard
  practical source" — never "moody and cinematic").
- Every registered asset has ID, status, origin, and license state; nothing
  stays in `inbox/`.
- Conflicts surfaced, never auto-resolved against approved canon.

## Common Failure Modes

- Treating mood-board inspiration as identity canon — binding level comes
  from the user, not from image quality.
- Describing the photo instead of the entity (the photo's lighting is not
  necessarily the character's canonical look — separate subject from
  treatment).
- Skipping license capture because the user "probably owns it".
- Building a LOOK from one image's incidental properties (JPEG artifacts,
  one odd white balance) instead of the batch's consistent signals.
- Ingesting a real person's likeness as a character identity without the
  clearance note commercial work requires
  (`rules/commercial/message-discipline.md`).

## Notes

Ingestion feeds `/visual-development`, not the other way around: analyze
first, then generate masters conditioned on the user's material. On
harnesses whose file tools read images (Claude Code, Cursor), analysis is
direct; where it isn't, the user pastes the images into chat and the skill
proceeds identically.
